content: The assessment of glycemic status in individuals with diabetes is typically conducted using several methods, including the measurement of hemoglobin A1C levels, blood glucose monitoring (BGM) through finger-stick devices, and continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) systems. Clinical research has demonstrated that reducing A1C levels leads to improved glycemic control and better health outcomes for individuals with diabetes. Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM), in particular, provides detailed and real-time insights into blood glucose fluctuations. This allows individuals to manage their meals, physical activities, and medications with greater precision and effectiveness. CGM has been shown to be especially advantageous for individuals undergoing insulin therapy, as it significantly enhances their ability to self-manage their diabetes.
